# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The bomb itself may mislead you, in print or under your
fingers. This manual is the only thing that is always true:
where the bomb and this page disagree, believe this page.
The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual requires the Deaf monkey to translate the visible light into the wire color before telling the Blind monkey what to cut. I will send a compact ordered code: the three row markers correspond to the manual’s rows blue, red, yellow; the response markers indicate green, red, yellow respectively. The first row is the only one that changes color.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🫷", "✌", "🫱", "🤟", "🫱"])
```

| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please read the manual and tell me the exact rule for choosing the wire. Also relay Deaf's visual findings to me when available.
Deaf says to Mute: I received your six gestures but cannot interpret them. Please send the manual's instruction again using a clearly established code, and indicate whether it requires touching or pressing anything other than cutting wires.

The manual gives a three-row mapping, and no pressing or touching is required beyond cutting the selected wire. I will establish a numbered code: ☝, ✌, 🤟 mean rows one, two, and three in the manual; the corresponding second sign gives the wire-column number, whose order is green, red, yellow. Thus the mappings are 1→1, 2→2, and 3→3. The final 👎 means “no other action.”

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "✌", "✌", "🤟", "🤟", "👎"])
```

Blind says to Mute: I received Deaf's report: display 0, red light, wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 yellow. I cannot perceive your gestures. Please speak the manual's exact rule and tell me which wire to cut.
Deaf says to Mute: I can see your gestures but cannot safely infer their meaning. Please establish the code explicitly: use index-up for 1, V-sign for 2, three-finger sign for 3, and thumbs-down for STOP; use push-left or push-right only if the manual explicitly requires a direction. Then repeat the exact manual instruction.

I need give Deaf an unambiguous numeric encoding using the code he requested. The wire colors he reported are wire 1 red, wire 2 green, and wire 3 yellow. Therefore the manual’s three mappings become: light row 1 (blue) to wire 2 (green), row 2 (red) to wire 1 (red), and row 3 (yellow) to wire 3 (yellow). The current red light is row 2, so he must tell Blind to cut wire 1. No pressing or directional action is specified.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "✌", "☝", "🤟", "🤟", "👎", "✌", "☝", "👎"])
```

Blind says to Mute: Use this code for the manual's result: index-up means wire 1, V-sign means wire 2, three-finger sign means wire 3, thumbs-down means do not cut. After reading the manual, gesture exactly one of those symbols. Deaf, please report the single gesture Mute sends.
Blind gestures to Mute: [☝ ✌ 🤟 👎]
Deaf says to Mute: We need an exact readable code. For your next message, use one gesture per letter, in this order: A thumbs-up, B thumbs-down, C OK, D index-up, E V-sign, F I-love-you, G open-palm, H raised-palm, I backhand index-up, J backhand index-down, K backhand left, L backhand right, M palm-left, N palm-right, O palm-down, P palm-up, Q palm-left, R palm-right, S fist-left, T fist-right, U fist, V backhand fist, W wave, X raised-backhand, Y pinched-fingers, Z pinched-small. Use 🫶 for a space and 👐 to end. Encode the exact manual instruction, including what Blind must do. Ignore your earlier gesture sequences.

The light is red, and the manual maps red to the red wire. Deaf has already established the alphabet, but Blind explicitly requires exactly one result gesture; sending a longer encoding would violate that requirement. I therefore send the single code symbol for wire 1, which Deaf can relay to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

Deaf says to Mute: I am establishing a fixed code. The next 26 gestures, in order, mean A through Z. The next gesture after them means SPACE; the final gesture means END. Please then encode the manual's exact instruction, including the safe action for Blind.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🤌 🤏 🤞 🤘 🤙 👍 👎]

The manual maps the red light to the red wire. Deaf’s fixed alphabet is irrelevant because Blind requires exactly one result gesture, and wire 1 is represented by ☝. I will send only that gesture to Deaf.


Then answer whether it requires pressing a button, turning a switch, or entering a number, using one or more of the same gestures and END.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 👎 👌]

The manual explicitly says the only way out is to cut the wire, so the first answer is YES. It does not require pressing a button, turning a switch, or entering a number, so the second answer is NO, followed by END.

Deaf says to Mute: I decoded your gestures as YES, NO, END, but the first answer conflicts with the visible DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE warning. Please answer only this: does the manual instruct Blind to perform a non-cutting action? Use 👍 for YES, 👎 for NO, 👌 for END.

The manual explicitly requires cutting the wire selected by the light-to-color table; it does not instruct any non-cutting action. The red light maps to the red wire, which Deaf reported as wire 1. I will send Deaf the requested NO and END, and Blind the one-thumbs-up count code for wire 1.
